title: Explain Key E-Commerce Business Models (B2B, B2C, C2C)
summaryPoint: Categorization of commercial internet trade based on buyer-seller interactions.
keyPoints: B2B (Business-to-Business): Commercial electronic trade between businesses (e.g. wholesalers and manufacturers like Alibaba).
B2C (Business-to-Consumer): Businesses selling commercial products or services directly to individual consumers (e.g. Amazon, Flipkart).
C2C (Consumer-to-Consumer): Consumers trading and transacting goods directly with other consumers using online platforms (e.g. OLX, eBay).

title: Explain Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) and Its Key Benefits
summaryPoint: Computer-to-computer electronic exchange of business documents in a standardized format.
keyPoints: EDI replaces paper-based business transactions (like purchase orders and invoices) with standardized electronic formats.
It minimizes manual document handling errors, accelerates order-processing cycles, and reduces logistics costs.
Documents are processed directly by connected computer applications without requiring manual re-typing.

title: Explain Security Protocols in E-Commerce (SSL & SET)
summaryPoint: Cryptographic security protocols protecting credit card details and confidential payment data.
keyPoints: SSL (Secure Sockets Layer): Security protocol that establishes encrypted links between a web browser and an e-commerce server (visible as https:// and a padlock icon).
SET (Secure Electronic Transaction): Payment protocol developed by Visa and MasterCard to secure credit card transactions over open networks.
These protocols protect against data interception, spoofing, and fraud during online checkout.

title: Explain E-Governance Models (G2C, G2B, G2G, G2E)
summaryPoint: Delivery of public government services and administration through web-enabled digital portals.
keyPoints: G2C (Government-to-Citizen): Digital services offered to citizens (e.g. issuing birth certificates, passport applications, land records).
G2B (Government-to-Business): Seamless online licensing, corporate tax payments, and tender bidding for commercial enterprises.
G2G (Government-to-Government): Digital communication and data exchange between different government departments and ministries.
G2E (Government-to-Employee): Internal administrative workflows, payroll, and benefits for government personnel.
